chunks: Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: “Allah has refused that anything be thought of the believer except good, and your breaking his bones, whether he is alive or dead, is the same.”

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer, whose dignity and sanctity are being affirmed
key_terms.خَيْرًا: good; the proper presumption concerning a believer
key_terms.سَوَاءٌ: the same; equal in ruling or sanctity in this context
key_terms.عِظَامَهُ: his bones; referring to bodily remains

ai.seo_question: Does Islam consider harming a believer’s body after death to be like harming it during life?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the sanctity and dignity of the believer, both in life and after death. It teaches ethical حسن الظن toward the believer and indicates a legal-moral equivalence in violating the believer’s bodily integrity whether alive or deceased.
